example.name: user_story_to_test
example.scenario: Translate a user story about login functionality into a Playwright test.
example.user_story:
As a registered user, I want to log in with my credentials so that I can access my personalized dashboard.
Acceptance Criteria: - Login form has username and password fields - Login button is enabled when both fields are filled - Successful login redirects to dashboard - Failed login shows error message

step.approach: Identify UI elements: - Username input field - Password input field - Login button - Error message container - Dashboard page (redirect target)
Create LoginPage class with: - Locators for username, password, button - Methods: navigate(), login(), verify_loaded(), get_error_message()
Create test_login.py with: - FN: documentation headers - Test for successful login - Test for failed login
step.artifact:
# FN:test_login.py """ FN:test_login.py Contains 1 class. Tests for Login functionality.
Primary: TestLogin.test_login_success
Classes: - TestLogin: Test suite for Login (lines 20-80)
Functions: - FN:test_login_success: Test successful login (lines 26-45) - FN:test_login_failure: Test failed login (lines 47-65) """
import pytest from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect from tests.e2e.ui.pages.login_page import LoginPage
class TestLogin: """FN:TestLogin - Test suite for Login functionality."""
def test_login_success(self, page: Page, base_url: str, login_payload: dict): """FN:test_login_success - Verify successful login redirects to dashboard.""" # Arrange login_page = LoginPage(page)
# Act login_page.navigate() login_page.login( login_payload["username"], login_payload["password"] )
# Assert expect(page).to_have_url("/dashboard") expect(page.get_by_text("Welcome")).to_be_visible()
def test_login_failure(self, page: Page, base_url: str): """FN:test_login_failure - Verify failed login shows error.""" # Arrange login_page = LoginPage(page)
# Act login_page.navigate() login_page.login("invalid", "wrong")
# Assert expect(login_page.get_error_message()).to_be_visible() expect(login_page.get_error_message()).to_have_text( "Invalid credentials" )

key_takeaways.takeaway: Page Objects encapsulate UI structure and interactions
Tests should be readable and document intent
Use fixtures for test data management

example.name: dashboard_test
example.scenario: Test dashboard functionality with data verification.
example.user_story:
As a dashboard user, I want to see my recent activities so that I can track my work.
Acceptance Criteria: - Dashboard displays activity list - Each activity shows title and timestamp - Activities are sorted by date (newest first)
example.test_implementation:
# FN:test_dashboard.py """ FN:test_dashboard.py Contains 1 class. Tests for Dashboard functionality.
Primary: TestDashboard.test_activities_display
Classes: - TestDashboard: Test suite for Dashboard (lines 20-70)
Functions: - FN:test_activities_display: Verify activities display (lines 26-50) """
import pytest from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect from tests.e2e.ui.pages.dashboard_page import DashboardPage
class TestDashboard: """FN:TestDashboard - Test suite for Dashboard functionality."""
def test_activities_display(self, page: Page, base_url: str, auth_fixture: dict): """FN:test_activities_display - Verify activities are displayed correctly.""" # Arrange dashboard = DashboardPage(page)
# Act - Navigate to dashboard dashboard.navigate(base_url) dashboard.wait_for_loaded()
# Assert - Activities are visible expect(dashboard.activity_list).to_be_visible() expect(dashboard.activity_items).to_have_count( auth_fixture["expected_activity_count"] )
# Assert - Activities have required fields first_activity = dashboard.activity_items.first expect(first_activity.get_by_test_id("title")).to_be_visible() expect(first_activity.get_by_test_id("timestamp")).to_be_visible()
